title: Reading Notes on the Treble Staff
subject: Music
objectives: Students will be able to name the line notes (E, G, B, D, F) and space notes (F, A, C, E) of the treble staff.
Students will be able to tell how many beats whole, half, and quarter notes get in 4/4 time.
targets: I can name notes on the treble staff.
I can count beats for whole, half, and quarter notes.
materials: Hand staff: students hold up a hand sideways, five fingers as five lines
Rhythm sticks or desks to tap

vocabulary.meaning: Five lines and four spaces where notes are written.
The G clef: its curl circles the G line, which names the other notes.
A note with a line through its middle.
A note sitting between two lines.

sequence.teacher: Play or sing a low note and a high note. Ask where each would sit on the staff.
sequence.students: Show low or high with their hands, then turn and talk.

slides.title: Warm-up
slides.prompt: Musicians write a high sound higher on the page. Why might that help someone read music?
slides.say: Listen for: you can see the tune go up and down.

sequence.teacher: Teach the staff, then the line notes and space notes with their sayings. Use the hand staff.
sequence.students: Point to lines and spaces on their hand staff; say the sayings together.

slides.say: Hold up a hand sideways: five fingers are five lines, and the gaps are the four spaces.

slides.title: Line notes

diagram.description: A treble staff with whole notes on each line, E, G, B, D, F, named under the staff.

slides.say: Have students make up their own saying for E G B D F; the silliest ones stick best.

slides.title: Space notes

diagram.description: A treble staff with whole notes in each space, F, A, C, E, named under the staff.

slides.say: Point out that F shows up twice (the bottom space and the top line) and E too (the bottom line and the top space). Sing the line notes, then the space notes, on a scale.

slides.title: Name it

diagram.description: A treble staff with one whole note on the second line (G).

slides.why: It's on the second line: E, then **G**.

sequence.teacher: Tap each note value while counting 1-2-3-4 aloud.

slides.title: How long does it last?

diagram.description: A one-line rhythm staff in 4/4 with a whole note, then a half note and two quarter notes, beat counts under each.

slides.callout: Two quarter notes last as long as one half note.
slides.say: Tap and count 1-2-3-4 aloud for the whole note; then half, quarter, quarter. Have the class tap it back.

sequence.then: Done? On the back, write a word using only space notes.
sequence.teacher: Students may use their hand staff. Read Q4 aloud for anyone who wants it. Collect every sheet when time's up.
Hand out sticky notes; students work on their own.
sequence.students: Draw and write on a sticky note.

slides.title: Exit ticket
slides.prompt: On your sticky note: draw a half note, and write how many beats it gets in 4/4.
slides.answer: An open note with a stem; 2 beats
slides.say: Notes with a filled-in head drew a quarter note: start there tomorrow.

checks: Is that note on a line or in a space?
How many beats does a half note get?

misconceptions.misconception: Counting lines and spaces together (calling the first space the second note).
misconceptions.response: Use the hand staff: name only fingers for line notes, only gaps for space notes.

misconceptions.misconception: Thinking a note above the staff is in the top space.
misconceptions.response: Draw the five lines first and check which gap the note sits in.

support: Give a staff card with E G B D F and F A C E written beside the lines and spaces.
Let students use the hand staff during the worksheet.
extension: Write a three-note word on the staff for a partner to read.
Name the note on the ledger line below the staff (middle C).
language: Point and say each letter name together.
Show the beats with taps, not only words.

walkthrough.think: Is each note on a line or in a space?
walkthrough.idea: Line notes from the bottom: E, G, B, D, F. Space notes: F, A, C, E.
steps: Note 1 sits on the bottom line: E.
Count up the lines: G, then B.
Note 4 is in the top space: E.

walkthrough.think: Which space is first? Count from the bottom.
walkthrough.idea: The spaces spell FACE from the bottom up.
steps: F is the first space from the bottom.
Whole notes are open ovals with no stem.
mistakes: Drawing the note on a line instead of in the space.

walkthrough.idea: Line notes are E, G, B, D, F, so BED is the only word spelled with them.
steps: FACE, CAFE, and ACE all use A or C, which are space notes.
B, E, and D are all line notes.

walkthrough.think: Tap it: how long do you hold a half note?
walkthrough.idea: In 4/4 time a whole note gets 4 beats, a half note 2, and a quarter note 1.
steps: Two quarter notes (1 + 1) last as long as one half note.
mistakes: Swapping half and whole: a half note is half as long as a whole note.

assessment: A student who has it names any line or space note on the treble staff, draws a note in a named space, and says how many beats whole, half, and quarter notes get.
